root_cause.text: A cleanup off-by-one bug in `drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c::setup_nic_devices()` caused the error-handling loop to skip destroying the NIC device at the failing index `i`, leaking memory on initialization failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the cleanup from `while (i--) { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); }` to `do { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); } while (i--);`, and the commit message explicitly says the current loop “skip[s] the failing index i, causing a memory leak.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the NIC device cleanup loop so the failed setup path always destroys the current device index, including when only one device was involved.
intent_record.what: The cleanup loop in setup_nic_devices() was changed from a pre-decrementing `while (i--)` loop to a `do { ... } while (i--);` loop, with the body and loop contents otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the failure-path cleanup behavior so the loop body executes at least once even when `i` is zero, ensuring the current NIC device index is logged and destroyed during cleanup instead of potentially skipping cleanup entirely.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes the off-by-one cleanup bug in setup_nic_devices() so the failing NIC device index is destroyed during error handling, preventing the memory leak.

candidates.rationale: This post-decrement loop skips the current failing index when cleanup begins at the first device (e.g., i == 0 or a single-device case), causing the error-handling path to miss destroying the NIC device that failed setup.

vuln_statements.explanation: This post-decrement cleanup loop skips the current failing index when error handling begins at the first device (including the single-device case), so the NIC device at the failing index is not destroyed and memory is leaked during initialization failure.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable cleanup loop is present and still uses the off-by-one pattern described in the root cause. In `setup_nic_devices()`, failure jumps to `setup_nic_dev_fail`, then `setup_nic_wait_intr:` executes `while (i--) { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); }`. Because `while (i--)` decrements before entering the body, if initialization fails at index `i`, the cleanup starts from `i-1` and skips destroying the NIC at the failing index itself. There is no compensating cleanup for the current `i` before the loop, so the bug is present. The shown code does not contain the fix; it does not destroy `i` on failure, only earlier indices.
